evidence.observation: The result claims “the rule stated in prose, table and the shape-match bullet; the example reuses a host”. In src/gnd/skills/gnd-model-from-text/references/unattended-growth.md:279-316, the JSON example lists only `policy` in `object_types` but gives `insurer` as a `subtype_links` subtype. The translator in tests/test_unattended_growth_guidance.py:54-69 resolves each subtype from the reply’s `object_types`, so this example raises KeyError. If `insurer` is instead an existing model type, setting its subtype link changes an existing element, contrary to the page’s additive rule. The test at lines 177-186 checks only the example’s field shapes.

concerns.recommendation: Make the example’s subtype link refer to a new object type in the reply, or remove it; validate the page’s actual JSON example through the reply translator.
concerns.title: The reply example cannot be translated as written

evidence.observation: GO5-C2 requires that “the empty one reports zero in every count”; close-results.md:57 repeats “the empty one is zero”. For a round without a proposal, src/gnd/evolve/summary.py:141-153 sets `rows` to None, `outcomes` to None and `shapes` to None. The returned summary therefore has null `outcomes` and `shape_matches`, while tests/test_go5_round_summary.py:144-150 asserts zero only for proposed, reused and added. The evolution contract at lines 460-463 documents the nulls, but close-delta.md lists no departure from GO5-C2.

concerns.recommendation: Either emit zero counts for an empty round or record an approved change to GO5-C2 and correct the close result and test to state which fields are null.
concerns.title: An empty round does not report zero in every count

evidence.observation: The result claims “equivalent Markdown reads the same”. The new reader in tests/support/markdown_sections.py:106-145 carries comment state across lines but carries no code-span state: an opening backtick with no same-line close is kept through line 139, then `<!--` on the next line starts a comment at line 140. A legal multiline code span such as `note followed by a newline and `<!--` is therefore read as a comment, potentially hiding the unchanged reply rule from tests/test_unattended_growth_guidance.py:331-360.

concerns.recommendation: Track code-span delimiters across lines in the Markdown reader and add a guard case with `<!--` inside a multiline code span.
concerns.title: The guidance guard misreads multiline code spans

evidence.observation: close-results.md claims 'eleven edits each fail the guard'. The cited test tests/test_unattended_growth_guidance.py::test_go4_t2_the_guard_fails_when_the_rule_is_removed (lines 367-386) is parametrized with 11 cases, but the third is ('Rows for a new fact type only', 'Rows for a new fact type only') with id 'noop-control': old == new, and the assertion is `assert bool(problems) == (old != new)`, so this case asserts the guard does NOT fail. Ten edits fail the guard; the eleventh is an explicit control that must not. GO4-C2 itself ('a guard test fails when the sentence is removed') is still met.

concerns.recommendation: Amend the GO4-C2 row to 'ten edits each fail the guard, plus a no-op control that does not', or drop the count and say 'each edit fails; a no-op control does not'.
concerns.title: GO4-C2 overstates the guard test: one of the eleven cases is a no-op control that must not fail

response.summary: Read the plan r4, close-results and close-delta, then the code and records each cites: _parsing.py's parse scope, outcomes.py's locator and closure, narrow.py, summary.py, policy.py, commands/evolve.py, tests/support/markdown_sections.py, the reply-shape and contract sections, the named GO1-GO5 tests and the round-summary fixtures. Criteria check out: D1's scope on handle is real, D4's refutation of GO5-C1 holds (additive_policy_issues never refuses an element ADD, so dropped-with needs a refused candidate, which writes no preview or shape matches), the known-mix fixture matches its README, t8-ratio.json records 0.31, the guard tests cover the Markdown variants, and the unreviewed commit ff67e11d code is total over the inputs it names (host-passed outcome lists are re-closed, hostile round files and unbound artifacts are refused by name). One accuracy slip in the close record: it claims eleven guard edits each fail, but one of the eleven parametrized cases is an explicit no-op control that asserts the guard does not fail.

evidence.observation: Verbatim: "| D5 | GO3 refuses by type first, then other outcomes, a preview without rows, the before model, rows that are not the operations in order | a dict cannot be asked for its digest; review GO3–GO5 F1 | GO3 spec §14, the evolution contract |". The listed refusals cover identity and binding, but not a before model outside the JSON data model. narrow_proposal (src/gnd/discover/narrow.py:47-54) checks the digest, then _before_document (narrow.py:85-90) returns json_document(parse_model_document(before_model.text.encode("utf-8"), source="model.orm.yaml")), and json_document raises ModelValueError (src/gnd/model/_documents.py:13-17, 27-61) for a YAML-only value. Reachable input: a preview refused at the current-model gate still writes the requested report (src/gnd/evolve/cli_service.py:736, 557-570; service.py:1778-1783 with stage="current-model", before_text set at service.py:1720-1723), so a workspace model that parses but fails validation on, say, a date value produces a report whose rows are all unassessed (service.py:454-481); narrow keeps every operation and escapes with ModelValueError('... holds a !!timestamp'), an exception none of the named refusals produces (narrow.py:38-54 raise only TypeError and three ValueErrors).

concerns.recommendation: Either add a named refusal to narrow_proposal for a before model json_document cannot spell (catch ModelValueError at narrow.py:90 and re-raise with the narrowing wording), or record in the GO3 spec and the contract's 'Narrowing a proposal' section that such a before model is refused by json_document's own error.
concerns.title: narrow_proposal escapes with ModelValueError on a before model outside the JSON data model

evidence.observation: Verbatim: "| D6 | GO5's summary binds every artifact by its own identity and keeps the host's text unstripped | review GO3–GO5 F4, F5 | the evolution contract \"Round summary\" |". The binding of outcome rows to the proposal's operations is weaker than GO3's: round_summary (src/gnd/evolve/summary.py:143-147) refuses rows whose "row.operation_index != position or row.operation_id != operation.operation_id" but never compares row.reference, while narrow_proposal (src/gnd/discover/narrow.py:49-54) refuses unless "row.reference != operation.locator.reference()" also fails to hold, and the contract's Round summary section (evolution-contract.md:467-469) states "rows that are not the proposal's operations, one per operation in order, are refused". The EvolutionOutcomeReport reader validates only ordering (models.py:996-999, _outcomes_cover with operations None), so a report row edited to carry another operation's reference passes into the summary's verdict counts.

concerns.recommendation: Add the reference comparison to the row check in summary.py:143-147 so both new APIs enforce the same documented rule, with a case beside test_r1_f2_outcomes_that_do_not_cover_the_proposal_are_refused (tests/test_go5_round_summary.py:252-255).
concerns.title: round_summary accepts outcome rows whose reference is not their operation's

response.summary: All three digests match. I read plan r4, close-results.md and close-delta.md, then the code and pages they rest on: src/gnd/model/_parsing.py, src/gnd/evolve/outcomes.py, service.py, cli_service.py, models.py, policy.py, src/gnd/discover/narrow.py, src/gnd/evolve/summary.py, src/gnd/commands/evolve.py, unattended-growth.md, the evolution contract, tests/support/markdown_sections.py and the five named test files. GO1-C1 to GO5-C4 are supported by tests that exist and assert what close-results claims; the cited evidence files exist (t8-ratio.json records 0.31; 002-phase-GO1.md; evidence/GO2-GO5/full-lane.md; notes/issue-replies.md drafts both replies and marks them unreleased). Delta rows check out against the code: D1 (the scope decorates gnd.commands.evolve.handle, commands/evolve.py:206), D2 (the whole-proposal dropped-with closure over the meta-schema walk, outcomes.py:281-371), D3 (policy.py:447-450 refuses any fact-type MODIFY outside provenance.rationale, so rows for an existing fact type route to open_questions), D5 and D6. D4's refutation holds: the additive policy admits every element ADD (policy.py:442-446) and refuses no element addition, so dropped-with needs a refused candidate, which writes no preview and no shape matches; the known-mix fixture README records the split. I read the ff67e11d code no reviewer had seen (narrow.py, summary.py, markdown_sections.py) line by line and probed the guarded-page reader for false passes; it fails closed on hidden, reflowed and retitled rules. Three advisory concerns follow, none blocking: one narrowing escape outside its named refusal list, one unchecked binding field in the summary, and missing close-record citations the plan's completion predicate lists.

criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if the delivered code does not do what the plan's goal and criteria claim, or a claimed result is not supported by the code, tests and records at this commit. "No concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.

The spec is the approved plan r4; rulings D7 and D8 are the owner's and are not re-argued. Check whether each criterion GO1-C1 to GO5-C4 is met by the code in src/gnd/model/_parsing.py, src/gnd/evolve/outcomes.py, service.py, cli_service.py, models.py, summary.py, src/gnd/discover/narrow.py and src/gnd/commands/evolve.py, by the pages unattended-growth.md and the evolution contract, and by the tests tests/test_go1_evolve_parse_once.py, test_go2_operation_outcomes.py, test_go3_narrowed_proposal.py, test_unattended_growth_guidance.py and test_go5_round_summary.py, as close-results.md claims.

Check the delta: is every listed departure true of the code, justified, and recorded where it says; is any departure from the plan missing from it? D4 refutes part of GO5-C1: check that its reasoning holds against src/gnd/evolve/policy.py.
close-delta.md names code no reviewer has read (commit ff67e11d: narrow.py, summary.py, tests/support/markdown_sections.py). Read that code especially.

Look for an input the change claims to handle that gets a wrong outcome or escapes as an exception other than the refusals each API names: proposals whose operations depend on each other in any order, validation issue paths, D-12 refusals, outcome lists a host passes back, round files, unbound artifacts, and Markdown edits of the guarded page.

Every regular expression, string split, slice and special-case branch the milestone added handles the whole class of input it is given, not only the examples in the tests and fixtures, and none reads structured text that a parser or an existing reader in this repository already reads.
Every concern's evidence must quote one of the three named artifacts; cite code and tests by path and line in the observation.
